 Democratic Senate Candidates Lead in Maine, Michigan, and Texas
 Ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, Data for Progress surveyed likely voters from October 23-27 in Maine , Michigan , and Texas , three battleground states that could determine control of the Senate.
 The surveys find Democratic candidates for Senate leading across all three states. Democrats also lead the Maine and Michigan governor’s races but trail narrowly in Texas.
 Maine 
 In Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson, a former Maine Senate president, leads Republican Senator Susan Collins 50% to 45% as Collins seeks a sixth term.
 In the governor’s race, Democrat Hannah Pingree, a former Maine House speaker, leads Republican Robert Charles, a lawyer, 49% to 37%, with Independent Rick Bennett at 7%.
 Michigan 
 In the race for Michigan’s open Senate seat, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, former executive director of the Detroit Health Department, leads Republican former U.S. Representative Mike Rogers 50% to 46%. The third-party candidates on the ballot each receive 1% of the vote or less.
 In the governor’s race, Democratic Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson leads Republican U.S. Representative John James 52% to 43%.
 Texas 
 In Texas, Democratic State Representative James Talarico leads Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton 49% to 45% in the race for Senate. Libertarian Ted Brown receives 2% of the vote.
 In the governor’s race, Republican Governor Greg Abbott leads Democratic State Representative Gina Hinojosa 48% to 47% as Abbott seeks a fourth term.
 In all three states, a majority of voters view both President Donald Trump and the Republican Party unfavorably. Views of the Democratic Party are more divided but still underwater, with net favorability −2 in Michigan, −4 in Maine, and −10 in Texas.
 These findings indicate that Democrats are competitive across the board, leading all three Senate races and two of three gubernatorial races polled, with the third, in Texas, within a single point.
